mainEntity.name: How much does a Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 turbo engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 turbo engine (H5H 490) costs £400-£1,200 supply-only, while a reconditioned unit is £1,200-£2,200 and a full rebuilt engine £2,000-£3,800 [ESTIMATED]. Fitted costs add £390-£520 labour at a specialist. Compare quotes through EnginesMarket to find the best deal for your exact year and mileage.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Symptoms include a rattling noise on cold start-up that may disappear as the engine warms, a check engine light with timing-related fault codes, and in severe cases, engine misfire or loss of power. The 1.3-litre turbo uses a timing chain with a hydraulic tensioner - if the tensioner loses pressure, the chain can stretch [EM-INTERVIEW].

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt H5H 490 engine costs around £2,000-£3,800 supply-only [ESTIMATED]. For a 2023-2025 ASX worth £15,000-£25,000, replacement is typically financially sensible - especially with a 12-month warranty. Always factor in labour (£390-£520) and the value of the car.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 turbo engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A specialist workshop typically completes a full H5H 490 engine swap in 8-10 hours. With parts sourcing and delivery factored in, allow 2-3 days from quote to car back on the road. Supply & fit options through EnginesMarket streamline the process by pairing you with a specialist who has the engine in stock.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 turbo and the previous 2.0-litre/2.4-litre ASX?

acceptedAnswer.text: The second-generation ASX (2023-present) is completely different from the previous model - it's built on the Renault CMF-B platform alongside the Captur, not in Japan . The 1.3-litre turbo engine produces 113-116kW and 270Nm, offering better fuel efficiency and more torque than the old 2.0-litre (110kW/197Nm) . The new ASX is also more expensive, reflecting its European build quality .

mainEntity.name: Does the Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 turbo have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 turbo (H5H 490) uses a timing chain, not a belt . This is confirmed by parts suppliers and workshop literature. The chain does not have a routine replacement interval, but can stretch on higher-mileage examples - particularly if oil changes are neglected. Use the correct 5W-40 oil specification to extend chain life .

historyTimeline.h2: Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 Turbo - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The second-generation Mitsubishi ASX, launched in 2023, marked a complete departure from the previous Japanese-built model. Built alongside the Renault Captur in Valladolid, Spain, it rides on the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi Alliance CMF-B platform and is powered by the Renault-sourced 1.3-litre turbocharged petrol engine . The ASX was discontinued in the UK in 2020, but the Renault-based model is expected to return to UK showrooms in 2026 .

commonProblems.h2: Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 Turbo Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 turbo (H5H 490) is a modern Renault-sourced engine with a timing chain, but it has known weak points that can drive replacement decisions: timing chain stretch, turbocharger cooling issues, and potential overheating. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - Why the Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 Turbo Timing Chain Wears
problems.rootCause: The 1.3-litre turbo engine uses a timing chain with a hydraulic tensioner . Extended oil change intervals or using incorrect oil viscosity (5W-40 is recommended) can lead to chain stretch and tensioner failure [EM-INTERVIEW]. Early warning signs include rattling noise on cold start-up and check engine lights.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, and VVT sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Catch it early when rattle first appears
When chain has stretched causing valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2023-2025 ASX 1.3 turbo is worth approximately £15,000-£25,000, with newer models retaining higher value [INDUSTRY ESTIMATE]. - Vehicle worth under ~£10,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£10,000-£18,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£18,000-£25,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £25,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: For a modern ASX 1.3 turbo, preventative timing chain replacement is strongly recommended when cold-start rattle appears - £800-£1,200 is far cheaper than a full engine replacement. Insist on the correct 5W-40 oil spec and avoid extended oil change intervals [EM-INTERVIEW].
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt H5H 490 Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 turbo engine prices

problems.h4: Turbocharger Cooling & Overheating - Why the Mitsubishi ASX 1.3 Turbo Suffers Cooling Issues
problems.rootCause: The 1.3-litre turbo engine's cooling system is shared with the Renault Captur. Reports indicate potential for coolant leaks from turbocharger cooling lines and water pump failure [THIRD-PARTY]. Overheating can lead to head gasket failure, particularly on vehicles driven hard or in hot climates .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Pressure test, coolant flush, replace faulty components
repairOptions.longevity: First port of call; effective if caught early

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace head gasket; machine head if warped
repairOptions.longevity: When cooling system failure has caused overheating
When head gasket failure has caused warping or bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2023-2025 ASX 1.3 turbo with 30k-60k miles is worth approximately £15,000-£22,000 [INDUSTRY ESTIMATE].
problems.recommendation: Regular coolant level checks and annual cooling system inspections are essential for this engine. If overheating occurs, stop driving immediately to avoid head gasket failure. For a higher-mileage ASX, a rebuilt engine with upgraded cooling components can be more cost-effective than repeated repairs [EM-INTERVIEW].
